summary: Binary exploitation: abuse a memory-safety bug in a program to hijack control flow or leak memory, usually to get a shell or read the flag. Workflow: triage protections -> find the bug -> build the primitive -> defeat mitigations -> exploit with pwntools.
quick_triage: checksec ./binary  -> which mitigations are on (Canary, NX, PIE, RELRO).
file ./binary and `./binary` once to see behavior; find the input that reaches the bug.
Decompile in Ghidra/radare2 to locate the vulnerable function (gets, read with bad size, printf(user), malloc/free pattern).
Identify bug class: stack overflow / format string / heap / integer / off-by-one.
Is libc provided? note its version (strings libc | grep 'GLIBC_') — it decides gadgets/one_gadget offsets.
Build + test the exploit LOCALLY against the provided binary before firing at remote.

tools.name: pwntools
tools.when: Every exploit — I/O, packing, ROP, shellcode, ELF/libc symbol lookup.
tools.usage: from pwn import *; p=process('./chall'); p.sendline(payload); p.interactive()

tools.name: gdb + pwndbg
tools.when: Dynamic analysis: inspect crash, stack, heap, find offsets.
tools.usage: gdb ./chall; pwndbg> cyclic 200; run; pwndbg> search-pattern; cyclic -l <val>

tools.name: GEF (gdb enhanced)
tools.when: Alternative to pwndbg; great heap/format-string helpers.
tools.usage: gef> checksec; gef> pattern create 200; gef> pattern search

tools.name: checksec
tools.when: First look: which mitigations are enabled.

tools.name: ROPgadget
tools.when: Find ROP gadgets (pop rdi, syscall, etc.).

tools.name: ropper
tools.when: Alternative gadget finder + ropchain builder; good search syntax.

tools.name: one_gadget
tools.when: Find single-shot execve('/bin/sh') gadgets in a libc.

tools.name: libc-database
tools.when: Identify remote libc from leaked symbol offsets; get base + gadget offsets.

tools.name: patchelf
tools.when: Make a provided libc/loader run with the binary locally for accurate testing.

tools.name: seccomp-tools
tools.when: Dump a binary's seccomp filter (which syscalls are allowed) — decides ORW vs shell.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.when: Decompile to C to understand the vulnerable logic quickly.

install.note: or download the release zip; needs JDK

tools.usage: Import binary -> auto-analyze -> read decompiled main()

tools.name: angr
tools.when: Symbolic execution: auto-solve input constraints, find path to win().

tools.name: objdump / readelf / nm
tools.when: Quick static look: sections, symbols, PLT/GOT, disassembly.

tools.name: PEDA
tools.when: gdb enhancement for exploit dev (alternative to pwndbg/GEF).

tools.name: libformatstr
tools.when: Build format-string write payloads quickly (helper library).

tools.name: Triton
tools.when: Dynamic binary analysis / symbolic execution when angr struggles on a concrete trace.
tools.usage: load a trace and solve path constraints symbolically
